title: Smoothness from a localization span in arbitrary universes
statement: For commutative rings R and A with an R-algebra structure, if a set s spans the unit ideal of A and every principal localization at an element of s is smooth over R, then A is smooth over R.

proof.text: Apply Mathlib Algebra.FinitePresentation.of_span_eq_top_target to s and hs, using the finitePresentation field of each smooth localization. This criterion is already universe-polymorphic.

By Mathlib Algebra.smoothLocus_eq_univ_iff, formal smoothness is equivalent to the smooth locus being all of Spec A. Rewrite the unit-ideal spanning hypothesis as the union of the basic opens being all of Spec A, using PrimeSpectrum.iSup_basicOpen_eq_top_iff'. Each basic open is contained in the smooth locus by Algebra.basicOpen_subset_smoothLocus_iff and the formallySmooth field of the corresponding hypothesis. Combine formal smoothness with the finite presentation obtained in the first step.

proof_origin.place: RingHom.Smooth.ofLocalizationSpanTarget: its finite-presentation and smooth-locus argument reused directly with separate universes

lean.statement: theorem smooth_of_localization_span_universes (R : Type u) (A : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] (s : Set A) (hs : Ideal.span s = ⊤) (h : ∀ g : s, Smooth R (Localization.Away (g : A))) : Smooth R A
